producing_commit.resolved_when: at process start, when Python bound the modules this run executed -- NOT at artefact assembly, which is a later tree
producing_commit.why_this_is_here: This run takes hours and the tree moves under it. A consumer that wants to publish these counts needs to know which code drew them, and no diff between two artefacts can supply that.

world_identity.what_this_identifies: the departure LEVEL the world was running at -- `year_level_anchor` for every year inside the published switching record, fitted and declared alike. Two runs sharing this digest ran over the same departure surface; two that do not are different worlds however close their timestamps, and no figure from one bounds a figure from the other.
world_identity.what_this_does_not_cover: the HOMES. `_published_departure_rates` is the observed switching record and does not know what houses this world contains, so a re-drawn housing stock cannot move this digest and provably has not: `39a192ce04c1eda8` spans the population of `3957ba848` and the population of this tree, which hold different homes. That question is the `homes` part beside this one, and this part alone is NOT the world.

homes.what_this_identifies: the HOME STOCK the world draws from -- 96 homes drawn through `net_new_acquisition.year_premise_stock`, the function a run's own homes come from, and then through the fabric physics, digested as every field of simulation.fabric_physics.FabricParameters. Two runs sharing this digest drew their homes from the same stock through the same physics; two that do not saw different houses, however close their timestamps and however well their departure levels agree.
homes.what_this_does_not_cover: WHICH homes a particular run drew. A run chooses its own seed, size and year mix, so two runs sharing this digest still hold different individual houses -- this says they came out of the same country, not that they are the same. It also covers only the FABRIC: a change to heating fuel, appliances or occupancy that leaves every thermal parameter alone does not move it, and the departure LEVEL is a separate part with its own digest.

book_identity.how_a_consumer_should_pair_this: Pair on `declared` and never on `realised_across_seeds`. The declared half is the book the run was given; the realised half is what the seed's own churn did to it, so two floors of the SAME book differ there by construction. A consumer that compared the counts would refuse every honest re-run.

what_this_is: The three-arm A/B re-run once per seed with ONLY the per-household elasticity assignment re-drawn. The spread below is the error bar on `selection_gbp` -- the figure the level-vs-selection split publishes.
redraw_key_means: the per-household elasticity assignment. Reached ONLY by households the value arm priced -- it sits behind an offered rate -- so the `except` half of this key is empty on this book and gets emptier as the arm prices more of it

redraw_scope.means: every household re-drawn -- the undecomposed floor, and the only mode whose spread bounds the published figure directly

symbol_resolution: read from `simulation.customer_events`'s own import statement, not written down here, so a rename disconnects this tool LOUDLY instead of silently returning a spread of zero

distance_to_a_sign.what_this_count_is: the seeds this family would need IF its mean and standard deviation stayed exactly where they are. New draws move both -- that is why they are worth taking -- so this is the price of the question at today's estimate and never a forecast that the sign will appear.
distance_to_a_sign.how_to_read_the_distance: `sems_from_zero` below `sems_needed_to_state_a_sign` means the sign is NOT stateable and says by how much. It is not a cue to re-run until a seed agrees (R12): the seed set is fixed before the draw and the answer is whatever it returns.

how_to_read_this: If the spread is WIDER than the published `selection_gbp`, the level-vs-selection instrument cannot yet resolve the question being asked of it, and every reading built on it carries that caveat. That is a finding about the INSTRUMENT and not about the pricing arm -- it is not a cue to re-run until a seed agrees (R12).

instrument_stamp.what_was_touched: NOTHING the producer wrote. This key was appended to the /var/tmp original on copy into docs/observability/; every other key is byte-equal to what `tools/run_value_cycle_ab.py` emitted at 2026-09-18T11:07:45Z. It is marked `added_after_the_fact` so it can never be read as the producer's own words.
instrument_stamp.why_a_stamp_at_all: This family is the LAST one drawn on a pricing instrument that has since been repaired. An unlabelled floor family is indistinguishable from a current one to anything that reads it, and pooling it with a post-fix family would contaminate precisely the quantity the repair moves.

the_instrument.name: two arms over UNEQUAL PRICED POPULATIONS
the_instrument.what_that_means: At this commit `company/pricing/value_based_renewal.py:decide_margin` is asymmetric by one bound. The VALUE arm FILTERS candidate margins on both the lawful ceiling and the churn-support bound (`lawful`, then `allowed`) and raises `MarginDecisionUnavailable` when `allowed` is empty -- so it can DECLINE. The LEVEL arm applies the lawful ceiling as a CLAMP (`min(level, headroom)`) and never applies the support bound at all -- so it prices every renewal it reaches. `selection_gbp = value_advantage_gbp - level_advantage_gbp` therefore differences two advantages earned over populations the arms do not share.
the_instrument.evidence_in_the_code: raise-on-empty-`allowed` is present at a178b56d6 (value_based_renewal.py:876) and absent at b329e702b.
the_instrument.departure_cost_term: PRESENT. `e1895d6c8` is an ancestor of this commit, so the renewal objective pays `-(1 - p_retain) * departure_cost_gbp`, with `replacement_cost_gbp` returning the sourced 27.50 GBP single-fuel PCS commission for resi and a DECLARED 0.0-with-a-reason for SME/I&C.

what_this_artefact_CANNOT_show_about_its.unavailable_because: This producer records no per-arm priced/declined counts in a floor artefact -- the seed rows carry `auc_population` (the VALUE arm's scored retained/left, ~105 of 154 settled billing accounts) and nothing for the level arm. The unequal-population asymmetry is therefore established from the CODE at the producing commit, above, and NOT measured inside this file. The 214-priced/281-priced, 64-decline figures on file elsewhere are from the three-arm runs over a 280-renewal book and are a DIFFERENT population from this floor's 154 settled billing accounts. They must not be read onto this artefact.

superseded_by.what_it_changed: gave the level arm the same evidence frontier, so the two arms price one book. The first run carrying it (docs/observability/value_cycle_ab_s1_three_arm_20260918.json) reads value 104 priced / 3 declined against level 107 / 3, `decision_population.same_priced_population: true`, and ZERO net refusals of renewals the other arm priced -- against 215/65 vs 281/0 before it.

pooling_rule.why_not: Those are a different instrument on exactly the axis this family is being read for. A mean over two instruments estimates neither -- the defect already filed against the previous published eighteen.
pooling_rule.same_instrument_test: `git diff c9bd2eae7 a178b56d6 -- simulation company saas tools/run_value_cycle_ab.py` is EMPTY -- the project's own four-path instrument test, applied consistently.
pooling_rule.even_then: The PRIMARY reading of this family is the twelve ALONE. A fifteen with auc3 was pre-registered before these seeds were readable and is reported as a labelled SECONDARY; it is wired into nothing.

the_reading.against_the_published_eighteen: The LEVEL replicates and the WIDTH does not. The published single-arm eighteen reads mean -959.78, sd 1631.80, sem 384.62, and states NEGATIVE at 2.50 sems. This family's mean sits 109.69 GBP from it -- 0.07 of this family's own sem -- while its sd is 3.31x wider (F = 10.94 on df 11,17; two-sided p = 2.3e-05). The published sign rests entirely on the width.
the_reading.the_artefacts_own_rule_fires: `how_to_read_this` in this file, written by the producer before any seed was readable: "If the spread is WIDER than the published `selection_gbp`, the level-vs-selection instrument cannot yet resolve the question being asked of it, and every reading built on it carries that caveat. That is a finding about the INSTRUMENT and not about the pricing arm -- it is not a cue to re-run until a seed agrees (R12)."
